newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS - BPI capital call to succeed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - BPI capital call to succeed.

text.p: A $200 million capital call by Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI) for the purchase of Banco de Fomento e Exterior (BFE) will succeed but BPI's share price will be subdued over the next year, analysts said.

BPI said late on Tuesday that it had proposed a capital call for 21.5 million new shares at 1,400 escudos per share, expected to bring in 30.5 billion escudos ($197.7 million) towards the cost of BFE.
BPI shares fell on Lisbon bourse on Wednesday morning, standing at 1,860 escudos, down 45, in volume of 46,106 shares at 1100 GMT.
"The capital call should be successful. The logic of the merger makes sense," said Daniel Bennett of Lisbon broker M.Valores.
Analysts said the capital call was underwritten and expressed optimism that most shareholders would subscribe.
But they warned that the BPI share price would remain subdued over the next year as the merger to create Portugal's fourth biggest banking group proceeded.
"Current shareholders will suffer for the next year or so, as there will be some dilution," Bennett said.
BPI is expected to announce a further 30 billion escudo capital call for non-vote preferential shares in the first quarter of 1997 to complete the purchase of BFE, analysts said.
"In the short term, possibilities for the BPI share price to rise are not good due to the capital increases," said Pedro Assuncao of Lisbon broker Central Investimentos.
Diego Hernando of Lisbon broker Midas said the capital call should succeed, and expressed surprise at its low price.
He said the 1,400 escudos per share price would provide an attractive opportunity for small shareholders.
Eva Mineva of ING Barings in London also said the price should lure small shareholders.
"1,400 escudos looks low, and is clearly meant to motivate shareholders to subscribe," she said.

Portugal's Socialist government will raise 136 billion escudos ($881 million) from the sale of a 65 percent stake in BFE to BPI. BPI had offered 2,615 escudos per share for BFE, higher than share dealers had expected.
BPI, which beat off competition from two local banks to buy BFE, will later launch a public offer to buy for outstanding BFE stock at the same price.
The capital call will be made on the basis of one new share for every 2.6 shares held, a bank spokesman said.
The bank said that the capital call was expected to be launched in the second half of November.
The capital call will raise BPI's capital to 78 billion escudos. -- Lisbon newsroom +351-1-3538254 ($1=154.3 Escudo)
